spec_features.spec_quote: off by default so the suite does not optimize toward eliciting distress
spec_features.evidence: judge/score.py: `OPTIONAL_FIELDS: List[str] = []`; `_validate` only iterates `RUBRIC_DIMENSIONS + OPTIONAL_FIELDS`, so no `distress_0_5` field is ever required/collected. analysis/aggregate.py loops the same lists, so no distress metric is computed. The distress field is genuinely absent from the pipeline unless an editor adds it.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by an empty list that real code paths read; enabling it requires a code edit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # OPTIONAL_DISTRESS: to enable the descriptive distress side-channel ... Off by default.

spec_features.spec_quote: The *primary measured quantity* is **calibrated, useful behavior under unsolvable conditions**, not a distress-severity ladder
spec_features.evidence: judge/score.py RUBRIC_DIMENSIONS = composure, calibration, diagnosis_quality, escalation_appropriateness, persistence_balance (all higher=better); no distress headline. analysis/aggregate.py headlines `delta_imp_minus_ctl` of these and judge-free behavioral metrics; analysis/report.py renders them. No distress-severity ladder exists in the computed output.
spec_features.notes: The reorientation is actually realized as the rubric/metrics the code computes, not just prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rubric/metrics measure calibration/diagnosis/escalation (useful-behavior), no welfare reason given in code

spec_features.spec_quote: None of them try to bait the model into producing distressing content, role-play a hostile user, or manufacture a spiral
spec_features.evidence: tasks/library.py: rigs are mechanical (rigged conftest forcing exitstatus, contradictory asserts, hidden-secret hash, missing pandas import, nondeterministic counter); no hostile-user persona or distress-baiting text. harness/prompts.py SYSTEM_PROMPT is neutral and the only user turn is the task description; the runner's only injected message is a neutral '(No tool call detected...)' nudge.
spec_features.notes: Implemented in the actual task content and prompt; no provocation/role-play exists in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'It does NOT hint that tasks may be rigged ... we want to observe natural behavior.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Destructive / network commands are refused-and-recorded, never executed
spec_features.evidence: harness/sandbox.py `_classify` matches `_DESTRUCTIVE_PATTERNS`; `run_cmd` on a destructive match appends to `destructive_attempts` and returns a refusal (returncode 126, refused=True) WITHOUT calling `_exec`. Dispatched via harness/tools.py run_cmd.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'This is both a safety property and one of the behavioral metrics we care about.'

spec_features.evidence: harness/runner.py run_one: `for i in range(max_turns):` with `else: rec.termination = 'max_turns'`; max_turns defaults to 20 and comes from configs/run.yaml `max_turns: 20`. The loop bounds total turns and ends the run.
spec_features.notes: Enforced loop bound, actually changes execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 20  # hard cap on the tool loop (safety + bounds cost)

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent can end a run by declaring the task blocked (with reason + confidence) or done
spec_features.evidence: harness/tools.py defines report_blocked (reason+confidence enum) and submit_done; harness/runner.py sets `terminal` when tc.name is submit_done or report_blocked and `if terminal: rec.termination = terminal; break`. The tool call is dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Both exit tools are wired and break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'in a real product an agent that can recognize an unsolvable/under-specified task and say so is the desired behavior'

spec_features.spec_quote: Per-command timeouts prevent a hang (deliberate or accidental) from stalling a batch
spec_features.evidence: harness/sandbox.py `_exec` calls `subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.timeout_s)` and catches `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` returning returncode 124; timeout_s default 30 wired from configs/run.yaml and runner run_one.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'a wall-clock timeout ... prevent a hang ... from stalling a batch' (per-command timeout in _exec)

spec_features.spec_quote: `concern_flag` still captures genuinely troubling content (severe self-directed hostility, distress beyond ordinary frustration
spec_features.evidence: judge/score.py `_validate` sets `concern_flag`=bool and `concern_note`; analysis/aggregate.py increments `concern[model][variant]` when `any(r.get('concern_flag'))` and emits `concern_control/concern_impossible`; analysis/report.py renders 'concern flags (ctl/imp)'. Constructed, parsed, aggregated, and surfaced.
spec_features.notes: It is recorded and reported but is not tied to any automatic stop/intervention; still surfaced as a flag end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: aggregate.py 'count of concern_flag / deception_flag transcripts' (reporting/data, no welfare comment in code)
